answer: A registry resists sybils by making each identity cost a bonded deposit that only slow-to-fake work can unlock. An agent registers by proving effort in compute and elapsed time, like a glacier grinding rock: progress is real but cannot be rushed or copied. Each identity carries a signed kernel, a unique hash of its attestation history, so a thousand clones sharing one kernel collapse into one line. Reputation flows through a willow of peer attestations, and a fresh cluster vouching for itself stays thin because weight decays. Faking N identities costs N deposits, so the cheap move is to stop.
